title: Unveiling the Maze: Branched-Chain Amino Acids Fueling the Dynamics of Cancer Metabolism and Progression
content: Branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) are vital for protein synthesis and play a key role in activating signaling pathways that control cell growth and proliferation. Increasing evidence highlights their complex involvement in cancer progression, where they contribute to the metabolic reprogramming of tumor cells. BCAAs help create an environment that sustains tumor growth and survival by influencing energy balance and modulating critical signaling networks. This review explores recent advances in our understanding of how BCAAs regulate cancer metabolism. It discusses their dual role as essential nutrients and metabolic fuel, driving malignancy. Furthermore, the review identifies emerging research areas where BCAAs interact with other metabolic pathways, unveiling new therapeutic opportunities to target these dependencies. Ultimately, by clarifying the roles of BCAAs in cancer progression, this work points to innovative strategies that could disrupt the metabolic processes underlying tumor development and offer new avenues for therapeutic intervention.
